Before entering upon this painful narrative, it may be proper to notice some incidents in Sikh history less important, but not with- out interest. In January, 1843, Dost Mahomed Khan, released from his confinement by the un- toward events in Afghanistan, in his progress towards Cabul through the Punjab, could do no less than pay a visit to the Maharaja at Lahore. Had his choice been perfectly free, he would probably have avoided an interview which, for many reasons, must have been
